Instead, we quantify properties by integrating over specific intervals, yielding directly interpretable counts or percentages. This approach avoids reliance on potentially misleading central tendency measures when distributions are skewed or multimodal. In modern contexts, these primitives map naturally to robust statistical inference: the percentile comparison becomes a Bayesian posterior check, while area-under-the-curve quantifies predictive uncertainty.
